Three steps, always: connect, read the table you want into a data frame, disconnect.

```{r db_connection}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(),
                     "../data/scout.db")
DBI::dbListTables(con) # get list of table names
postings = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "scout_postings") # read the specific table you want
DBI::dbDisconnect(con) # disconnect from the database
dplyr::glimpse(postings[, c("title", "company",
  "location_state", "remote", "skills_json")]) # glimpse of the specific columns

first_cell = postings$skills_json[1]
cat(strtrim(first_cell, 60))   # base R: first 60 characters


skills = jsonlite::fromJSON(first_cell) # read JSON text and convert it into an R object
skills


dplyr::glimpse(postings)
```

## usethis::edit_r_environ()


```{r sql}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(),
                     "../data/scout.db")

#dbGetQuery - runs an SQL query and returns the results to R
top_remote = DBI::dbGetQuery(con, " 
  SELECT company, COUNT(*) AS n
  FROM scout_postings
  WHERE remote = 1
  GROUP BY company
  ORDER BY n DESC
  LIMIT 10") # stop after 10 rows, return only first 10 results
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
top_remote
```
